about: Cross-implementation CAN protocol vectors. Every URTC client that implements a vector must reproduce it byte for byte. Hex strings have no separators; ids are written 0xNNN. A vector may carry a note when the readers are allowed to differ. The sections up to version_order are written by hand; identifiers_all, frames_encode, frames_decode, frames_rejected and slcan_stream are generated from spec/can_protocol.json by tools/make_conformance.py.

slcan_decode.name: DLC 9 is not a CAN 2.0 frame
DLC F is not a CAN 2.0 frame
extended frame whose 29-bit id looks like 0x111
adapter timestamp after the payload
slcan_decode.note: Adapters with timestamps enabled append 4 hex digits after the payload. This protocol never enables them, so the readers may differ here; each client documents what it does.

quick_state.name: four-byte answer from firmware before the thermal guard
five bytes: thermal fault, no reset cause
six bytes: power-on reset, boot sequence running
three bytes is not an answer

version_query.name: application that predates the patch frame
patch 0xFF means unknown but the board is patch-aware
bootloader with 0x7FA and a patch frame announcing the end-update patch
patch frame longer than 3 bytes: extra bytes ignored
patch frame shorter than 3 bytes is not a patch frame
version answer shorter than 8 bytes gets no answer
